facts.raw_span: A 75-year-old Caucasian woman was admitted with a prosthetic hip infection 10 days after revision surgery
hypertension, type 2 diabetes, heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and folate deficiency
pulse 80/min, respiratory rate 24/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air
Sodium 142 mmol/L, potassium 3.5 mmol/L, chloride 118 mmol/L, bicarbonate 5 mmol/L
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.18, pCO2 1.7 kPa, pO2 16.7 kPa, bicarbonate 8.3 mmol/L, base excess –22.7 mmol/L
A 75-year-old Caucasian woman was admitted with a prosthetic hip infection 10 days after revision surgery
hypertension, type 2 diabetes, heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and folate deficiency
pulse 80/min, respiratory rate 24/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air
Sodium 142 mmol/L, potassium 3.5 mmol/L, chloride 118 mmol/L, bicarbonate 5 mmol/L
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.18, pCO2 1.7 kPa, pO2 16.7 kPa, bicarbonate 8.3 mmol/L, base excess –22.7 mmol/L

concepts.why: The patient has a history of type 2 diabetes and presents with metabolic acidosis, as evidenced by the low bicarbonate level and high anion gap.
The patient has a high anion gap and low bicarbonate level, consistent with lactic acidosis, and the lactic acid level is elevated.
The patient has a prosthetic hip infection and presents with signs of sepsis, including tachypnea and altered mental status.
The patient has a history of chronic kidney disease and presents with metabolic acidosis, which may be contributing to acute kidney injury.
The patient is taking multiple medications, including vancomycin and acetaminophen, which may be contributing to altered mental status.
The patient has a history of COPD and presents with tachypnea and hyperventilation, consistent with an exacerbation.
The patient has a history of folate deficiency, which may be contributing to the presentation.
The patient has a history of heart failure, which may be contributing to the presentation.
The patient has a high corrected anion gap of 25 mmol/L, indicating the presence of metabolic acidosis.

rationales.F01: Prosthetic hip infection may be related to sepsis.
rationales.F02: Chronic kidney disease may contribute to acute kidney injury.
rationales.F03: Multiple comorbidities increase the risk of various conditions.
rationales.F04: Drowsiness, confusion, and disorientation may be related to medication-induced encephalopathy or lactic acidosis.
rationales.F05: Glasgow Coma Scale score of 12 indicates altered mental status, which may be related to medication-induced encephalopathy.
rationales.F09: Electrolyte imbalance may contribute to metabolic acidosis.
rationales.F10: Arterial blood gas results indicate severe metabolic acidosis.
rationales.F11: Corrected anion gap is elevated, indicating metabolic acidosis.
rationales.F12: Normal lactic acid level rules out lactic acidosis and diabetic ketoacidosis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's arterial blood gas results (pH 7.18, bicarbonate 8.3 mmol/L, base excess –22.7 mmol/L) and corrected anion gap of 25 mmol/L strongly support the diagnosis of metabolic acidosis, which explains the patient's drowsiness, confusion, and hyperventilation.
